channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: NewsBlur rebuilds its mobile web reader
item.description: NewsBlur replaced its long-neglected mobile site with a responsive version of the desktop reader. The rewrite shares one codebase, adds touch-friendly layouts and swipe gestures, respects the browser back button, and makes the feed list paint immediately—useful progress for an independent, web-native RSS reader.

item.title: Feeder counts more than 300,000 recently active RSS feeds
item.description: Feeder’s newly updated answer to “Is RSS dead?” uses its own index as evidence: more than 300,000 followed feeds published something in the previous 30 days. The article also maps RSS’s quiet infrastructure role across publishers and podcast apps, a measurable counterpoint to recurring declarations that the format has vanished.

item.title: Public media faces a choice beyond simply restoring federal funds
item.description: With a new Congress arriving January 3 after the Corporation for Public Broadcasting’s dissolution, Nieman Lab examines whether lawmakers should recreate the old system or build something more local and democratic. Proposals include public media centers governed by communities rather than another return to the previous structure.

item.title: Reddit ends RSS support without a general replacement
item.description: Reddit’s November changelog says RSS support ended November 13. The company offers no replacement for feeds outside moderated communities, directing moderators to a Discord relay for some alerts. The change removes a longstanding read-only bridge between Reddit and independent feed readers.

item.title: Indie software needs financing built for durable small businesses
item.description: Ben Werdmuller argues that many useful independent tools were pushed toward venture-scale growth they could never sustain. He makes the case for bootstrapping, recurring revenue, revenue-based investment and community support that rewards durable services instead of demanding an unlikely giant exit.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 Field Guide details more than 440 core changes
item.description: The WordPress 7.2 Field Guide turns the release candidate into a practical developer checklist: more than 440 Core tickets, roughly 150 enhancements, 260 fixes and 40 editor issues. Highlights include SVG admin icons, a /random/ endpoint, SQL-mode work and preparation for jQuery 4.

item.title: Webnerd News turns open-web discovery into follows and shared feeds
item.description: Louis Gray’s new news view starts with user-chosen RSS feeds and transparent topic bundles, then adds one-click following and sharing to a public RSS stream. The design treats discovery as a path to lasting subscriptions and outbound traffic rather than another closed destination governed by a ranking algorithm.

item.title: ICANN opens public review of 1,610 proposed top-level domains
item.description: ICANN published the final application list for its 2026 generic top-level-domain round and opened comments and formal objections through March 16, 2027. The process includes 1,610 applications and 226 contention sets, giving the public a rare chance to flag confusion, legal-rights or community concerns before evaluation.

item.title: Static Radio builds a live dial from independent podcast feeds
item.description: A two-person Chicago studio has launched Static Radio, a free app with nine always-on stations assembled from roughly 1,000 independent podcasts. Everyone hears the same moment, but episodes stream in full from publishers’ own RSS feeds, preserving download attribution while replacing search and recommendation feeds with human curation.

item.title: WordPress 7.1.5 closes 20 security holes and urges immediate updates
item.description: WordPress released 7.1.5 with fixes for SQL injection, privilege escalation, cross-site scripting, REST and XML-RPC information disclosure, and a Template Part flaw that could lead to remote code execution. Maintainers recommend updating immediately; applicable fixes are also being backported through branch 4.7.

item.title: Entrepreneurs On Fire sells for up to $9 million
item.description: The independent business podcast Entrepreneurs On Fire has been sold to Pathos Communications for $3 million in cash plus as much as $6 million in performance payments. Founder John Lee Dumas will remain host for at least three years, making the deal a revealing valuation of a profitable, personality-led podcast brand.

item.title: Archive Team races to preserve Apple’s support forums before Friday shutdown
item.description: Archive Team lists Apple Discussions as an urgent preservation project before the Apple Support Community closes November 20. The user-to-user troubleshooting archive dates to the 1998 Apple Tech Exchange, making the rescue an unusually large effort to retain practical personal-computing history that Apple has not promised to keep online.

item.title: WordPress 7.2 reaches its first release candidate
item.description: WordPress 7.2 RC1 is available for testing ahead of the December 8 final release. Recent fixes cover media uploads, accessibility, revision previews, plugin dependencies and the Interactivity API; plugin and theme authors are urged to complete compatibility testing without using RC1 on production sites.

item.title: Overcast tests manual ad skipping while trying to protect creators
item.description: Independent podcast app Overcast is testing Smart Skip for premium users. It detects an ad break but never skips automatically, stops before the final call to action and ignores a show’s own membership or product promotions—an attempt by developer Marco Arment to meet listener demand without undermining open-feed economics.

item.title: A 10,000-site crawl finds RSS alive but increasingly hidden
item.description: A crawl of the 10,000 most popular domains found a discoverable working feed on 24% of readable sites. RSS accounted for 94% of working feeds, but 57% of sites that advertised one in 2016 no longer do; several still update the old address, suggesting feed discovery has declined faster than feed publishing.
